pr_title: Fix stack leniency not applying immediately after change
pr_body:
RFC. Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/20675.

I don't love this diff and I'm a bit scared of this change, but the last time this was attempted to be fixed the end result was https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/25467, so in comparison this looks like it may have a chance of maybe passing review.

Will add some self-review comments in a sec because this is a bit counterintuitive and I wasn't sure how much of this was deserving comments (provided this diff survives the initial eye test even). Can also try and add tests for this if this is deemed a viable route forward.

issue_context.title: Stack leniency doesn't affect objects immediately in Editor
issue_context.body:
### Type

Cosmetic

### Bug description

Stack leniency setting works only after editor reloading. Has no visual effect without reloading.
On screen no stacking after map loaded with stack leniency 0 and then adjusted to 1.0. But stacking is enabled after reloading.

### Screenshots or videos

![изображение](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/55319814/194791499-6b58fa4d-4b45-4394-b6f3-cfdb139afc56.png)


### Version

osu! 2022.1008.2-lazer

comments:
This can be easily noticeable by using a debugger and breakpointing at the point of applying stack positioning. It's happening due to the beatmap that `BeatmapProcessor` uses belonging to `PlayableBeatmap` rather than `EditorBeatmap`, causing the states to not sync immediately. One way to fix this would be to let the processor use the separate `BeatmapInfo` instance via constructor ([diff](https://github.com/ppy/osu/compare/master..frenzibyte:osu:fix-stack-leniency)).

But this begs the question of why `PlayableBeatmap.BeatmapInfo != EditorBeatmap.BeatmapInfo` in the first place, seems like a huge oversight as there's nowhere mentioning any reason why.

review_comments:
This is the primary fix and it works by addressing the thing mentioned in https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/20675#issuecomment-1279742039, namely reading from the correct `BeatmapInfo` instance.

I audited both beatmap processors of ours that actually do stuff (osu! and catch), and all of the properties they touch aside from `BeatmapInfo` are proxied in `EditorBeatmap` forward to `PlayableBeatmap`, so from that angle this seems *safe-ish*.

This hard cast needs to be gone for the `EditorBeatmap` change to have a chance of working, because `EditorBeatmap` is not a `Beatmap<OsuHitObject>`. The catch processor strangely does not do this sort of casting and does nice proper soft casts instead.

As an "optimisation" (reducing iterator and list allocations) I added the soft-cast of `Beatmap.HitObjects` to `List<OsuHitObject>`.

This bypasses the following guard:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/a8a2e543d51788b1dc05ab318b54b46af76d0be7/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/EditorBeatmap.cs#L349-L350

Compare:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/a8a2e543d51788b1dc05ab318b54b46af76d0be7/osu.Game/Screens/Edit/Setup/DifficultySection.cs#L119-L132
